changes.before: Turn one idea into one change you can see at work. Name a small first step, a real moment to try it, and a date thirty days out to look back.
changes.after: Connect one learning insight with a next step within your responsibility. Identify what you need to retain, examine or revise, who should be involved, and when to review the result. The form starts with a thirty-day review date; adjust it to fit the work.

changes.before: Why a plan this small works
changes.after: Make the plan specific enough to review

changes.before: Change sticks when it is specific, tied to a moment you already face and reviewed soon after. A single behavior you try three times teaches more than a long list you never start. The review questions help you separate what you observed from what you hoped, and decide whether to keep, adjust or stop.
changes.after: A specific step gives you something to examine later: what you did, what happened, and what remains uncertain. Use the plan to prepare rather than to claim authority or predict success. Follow required review and approval processes before changing actual work, and use the review to decide whether to retain, adjust or stop an approach.
